ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed shareholders, directors, managers, and natural-person UBOs against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists and ISIL/AQ Sanctions; (ii) US OFAC SDN and non-SDN Sectoral Sanctions Lists; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) UK HMT Consolidated List; (v) Egypt's Ministry of Justice designated terrorist entities and persons (Law No. 8 of 2015); (vi) Interpol Red Notices and watchlists. PEP status for domestic political-office holders, foreign prominent public functions, and senior SOE executives is processed under FATF Recommendations 12 and 25; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, and senior-management approval are mandatory for PEPs and for any UBO relationship above 25%. PEP risk persists for 12 months after leaving public office. All screening outputs must be retained for five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI 'Egypt for Investment' One-Stop Shop portal (www.gafi.gov.eg / investinegypt.gov.eg) and the Egyptian Commercial Registry database of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The operative statutory name must be rendered in Arabic script; the Arabic name is the legally registered name. An English transliteration may be registered as a secondary name. The proposed name must not be identical, similar, or phonetically conflatable with an existing registered name or trademark, must accurately reflect the LLC legal form, and must not mislead as to the nature, geography, or state affiliation of the business.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Islamic / إسلامي (religious reference requiring prior approval)
Investment / استثمار (licensing as investment company required)
Capital / رأسمال or كابيتال (capital-market connotation requiring FRA consent)
Royal / ملكي and Sultan / سلطان (sovereign and feudal titles)
Terms implying state patronage, political party affiliation, or foreign state sponsorship without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: GAFI issues a written rejection notice stating the legal grounds. The applicant, through the formation law firm, may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 business days of rejection, attaching a trademark search certificate from the Egyptian Trademark Office and a revised transliteration or distinctive-token strategy. If rejection is based on a sensitive token, the file is routed to the competent minister/authority for conditional consent. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may (i) re-submit under a different distinctive Arabic name, or (ii) challenge the decision before the Economic Administrative Courts under the Council of State. Rejection does not refund the clearance fee, and the reservation must be renewed after expiry of the 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not viable as the sole presence for ISIC 1080 pet-food manufacturing: the industry requires a physical factory and industrial premises approved by the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) and a food-safety license from the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) in addition to veterinary clearance from GOVS. A virtual office may serve only as the registered administrative address for service of notices, but GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a notarized lease or title deed for the actual production facility and fixed offices in Egypt; pure virtual-office arrangements are rejected for manufacturing LLCs.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (85-95%): NFSA under Law No. 1 of 2017 conducts unannounced food-facility audits; the Egyptian Regulatory Authority for Veterinary Services and the Ministry of Health inspect animal-origin raw meat supply chains; GAFI and Commercial Registry inspectors may verify the registered office; Ministry of Manpower occupational-safety inspectors visit industrial facilities routinely. Full UBO documentation and premises records must be maintained on-site in Arabic and presented upon request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, Articles 1, 6, 7, 24, 57–66; Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96/1982); Investment Law No. 72/2017, Articles 13 and 17, as administered by GAFI; Commercial Registry rules under Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration and Investor Service Center, Cairo; Commercial Registry Office of the relevant governorate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (MOA/AOA) in Arabic, executed before a public notary and submitted through GAFI's electronic establishment form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Egyptian LLC under Law 159/1981; capital is determined in the MOA. The full subscribed capital must be deposited in an Egyptian bank account before notarization, or supported by a licensed in-kind valuation. Funds are held under an escrow-type acknowledgement until GAFI issues the incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Memorandum and Articles of Association are adopted. The subscribers in Annex A are allotted [ ] ordinary shares of [EGP] each as paid-up capital, per the approved subscription schedule. The registered office is established at [address], Cairo, Egypt. [Name] and [Name] are appointed authorized signatories to execute statutory filings, bank and escrow operations, tax/environment registrations, and employment documents. All officers shall obtain the industrial operating license from IDA and food safety permit from NFSA. The Compliance Secretary shall file the incorporation dossier with GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and legal due diligence on proposed company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Service Center (ISC) – electronic name reservation system in coordination with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online 'Name Reservation' request through GAFI's one-stop shop, specifying ISIC 1080 freeze-dried pet food manufacturing activity. Pay the nominal reservation fee and obtain the availability certificate. Do not draft the MOA until the name is provisionally reserved; include Arabic and English transliteration for later bank and license matching.
required_dossiers: Proposed Arabic and English company name with transliteration
Copy of shareholders' national ID or passport
Simple activity description: manufacture of vacuum freeze-dried raw meat pet treats and meal kibble
Covering letter addressed to GAFI Name Reservation Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited wording, file a written administrative inquiry with the Commercial Registry name unit; provide three alternative names and resubmit without an additional fee within two working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and authentication of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary (Katib al-Adl) in the governorate of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage licensed corporate counsel to draft the Arabic MOA/AOA with precise capital, share distribution, business scope, management powers, and quorum rules. All shareholders, or holders of a valid power of attorney, must sign in person before the notary. The notary authenticates signatures and pagination, making the instrument the foundational document for GAFI and Commercial Registry filings.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft MOA/AOA in Arabic prepared by counsel
National ID or passport of each shareholder and manager
Power of attorney in Arabic or bilingual with consular attestation for non-resident shareholders
Proof of capital deposit or independent valuation report for in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a technical defect in the capital clause or signature authority, amend the relevant article and re-execute before the same notary; for an absent shareholder, obtain a legally attested power of attorney and re-notarize the instrument without a new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company incorporation filing with GAFI one-stop shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / Online Establishment Portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized MOA/AOA and supporting documents to GAFI's 'Investor Services' electronic portal as one PDF package. Complete Form 1 (Application for Establishment of an Egyptian Limited Liability Company), select ISIC 1080 with the description 'Vacuum Freeze-Drying Manufacture of Organic Pet Treats and Meal Kibble', pay official fees through the bank or at the OSS podium, and track the application. After provisional approval, submit physical originals for barcode scanning and OSS verification.
required_dossiers: Notarized MOA/AOA original and two certified copies
GAFI Form 1 electronic acknowledgement
Name reservation certificate
Bank deposit certificate or authentication of in-kind capital
Registered office lease contract
Corporate passports/photos for officers, if required at physical submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a 'necessity query' for incomplete documents or missing barcode data, respond with legal counsel within 15 working days; if rejection is issued, appeal to the GAFI Investor Grievance Committee under Investment Law 72/2017, attaching the original rejection note and corrective explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Commercial Registry and with the Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the relevant governorate; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Central Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified GAFI incorporation certificate and notarized MOA/AOA with the Commercial Registry to obtain the commercial registration number and extract. Then submit ETA Form 1 for the Unified Tax Card and obtain the tax identification file. Present the board resolution appointing officers and the registered office lease to the clerk. Corporate income tax is not triggered until revenue generation, but registration is mandatory from formation.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate (provisional or final)
Certified MOA/AOA
Board resolution appointing officers and authorized signatories
Registered office lease or title deed
Passports and photographs of directors/managers
Commercial Registry application form and ETA Form 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requests additional proof of physical office, provide the notarized lease and a National Address stamp; if ETA refuses registration pending NFSA credentials, obtain a written registration hold notice and complete NFSA registration before resubmitting ETA Form 1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account activation, social insurance and labor registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt; National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name using the board resolution, incorporation certificate, commercial registry extract, tax card, and signatory passports. Transfer or maintain the subscribed capital in an escrow-linked current account. Within 14 days of account activation, register the company and its employees with NOSI. Execute an additional bank signatories resolution and affix the company seal, if adopted.
required_dossiers: Original incorporation certificate and commercial registry extract
Board resolution specifying bank signatories and transaction limits
Unified tax card
Lease agreement for bank address due diligence
Employment contract templates and payroll list for NOSI registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests a GAFI post-formation 'company file certificate', apply to the GAFI post-registration window and present the original deposit certificate; if NOSI delays acceptance, file Form 1 with a stamped receipt and submit a written compliance note referencing the mandatory insurance law response deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtainment of industrial operating license, environmental and civil-defense clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – Licensing Center, Ministry of Trade and Industry; National Food Safety Authority (NFSA); Egyptian Civil Defense Authority for fire safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a consolidated application to IDA's 'Industrial Operating License' dossier, including site plan, freeze-driver machinery layout, food safety plan, EIA clearance, and Civil Defense certificate. NFSA inspects the processing line and storage area for HACCP-aligned raw meat handling. The final industrial license must be displayed at the factory site before production commences.
required_dossiers: EIA clearance or environmental registration from the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA)
Civil Defense certificate for fire suppression, egress, and structural load
Site plan and industrial usufruct/title certificate
HACCP/PET food safety manual with hazard analysis for raw meat
GAFI incorporation certificate and commercial registry extract
Unified tax card and NOSI registration certificate
Facility water and product handling health certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IDA or NFSA requires additional environmental controls, submit a corrective action plan within 60 days; if a license condition is contested, appeal in writing to IDA's general directorate or NFSA technical committee; production may not begin before the final license and clearance certificates are issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Licensing Center, Ministry of Trade and Industry; establishment and operation of a pet food production facility on Egyptian territory requires an industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License (رخصة تشغيل صناعى) for Production of Pet Food / NFSA Food Facility Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B / C: Freeze-dried pet treat and meal kibble plants require an Environmental Screening Report (EIA-B) for small/medium lines; a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report (EIA-C) is mandatory if the facility is located near water bodies, residential buffers, or protected areas, or if raw meat throughput exceeds medium-class thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Law No. 93/1962 and Ministerial Decree No. 92/2015 for sewer discharge limits (COD ≤ 750 mg/L, BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 400 mg/L where applicable to industrial food processing). Air emissions from freeze-drying vacuum pumps and any volatile organic compounds must remain within ambient air quality limits under Egyptian Air Pollution Standards. Solid waste handling and classification shall follow Waste Management Law No. 202/2020; vacuum-pump oils and refrigerant gases must be recovered by licensed waste vendors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority approval is required for fire detection and suppression systems, non-combustible storage layout, two unobstructed egress exits, and structural load inspection of the freeze-dryer installation. Ministry of Manpower occupational medical and workplace safety certificates are required, covering machine guarding, noise and dust exposure limits, employee protective equipment, and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) operating under the Egyptian Ministry of Finance; official taxpayer portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing platform: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg; Egyptian Customs single window (NAFIZA): https://www.nafiza.gov.eg; investment and company registry administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI): https://www.gafi.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the EG LLC through the GAFI One-Stop Shop under Companies Law 4/2018, obtaining the Commercial Register certificate and industrial/GOEIC activity license for freeze-dried pet-food manufacturing; 2) Within 30 days of commercial registration, file the unified ETA Tax Registration Form (Form 1) together with the GAFI incorporation package, notarized Articles of Association, Commercial Register extract, registered-lease proof, director/UBO identity documents and powers of attorney; 3) The ETA issues a single unified Tax Identification Number (TIN and tax card) covering corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax and payroll tax, with the VAT registration activated simultaneously when projected annual taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000 or earlier at the exporter's request for input-VAT recovery; 4) Register as an exporter in the Egyptian Customs NAFIZA system to obtain the customs exporter code; 5) Open an export-proceeds account with a Central Bank of Egypt (CBE)-licensed bank to satisfy the 180-day foreign-currency repatriation requirement; 6) Apply on the ETA e-invoicing portal for the digital-signature certificate and API integration credentials (client identifier and secret) mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The EG LLC is a juridical person subject to Egyptian corporate income tax at 22.5% on worldwide taxable income, with a foreign tax credit for foreign-source income; no fiscal transparency is available. Shareholders are taxed separately: a final 10% withholding tax applies to dividends actually distributed, and for an LLC retaining after-tax profits without a distribution resolution within six months of the fiscal year-end, the ETA imposes a 10% deemed-dividend tax on 50% of the net after-tax profit. Egypt applies a unitary national tax system with no sub-national income tax distinction. The standard onshore classification is applied in this dossier; an alternative elective free-zone status (e.g., Suez Canal Economic Zone) under Law 83/2002 would be a separate investment decision and is not the default classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch entity election; the LLC is classified as a taxable corporation by statute. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal-year-end election (calendar-year default, subject to prior ETA approval); (ii) Small Business Tax Regime election under Law 25/2020 applying a final presumptive turnover-based tax for annual turnover of EGP 500,000 to EGP 2,000,000, generally unsuitable for an export manufacturer because input-VAT recovery is forfeited; (iii) dividend-resolution election, whereby the shareholders resolve an actual distribution within six months of the fiscal year-end, activating the 10% final withholding tax and avoiding the ETA deemed-dividend tax on retained profits; (iv) VAT input-apportionment election for mixed-use expenses, subject to ETA approval; and (v) a CBE-approved extension election for the 180-day export-proceeds repatriation deadline in exceptional force-majeure circumstances.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value Added Tax introduced by Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree 1479/2016); single national regime administered by the ETA, territorial scope covering goods supplied and services rendered within Egypt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and services triggers mandatory VAT registration (VAT Law 67/2016, Article 27). An export-oriented freeze-dried pet-food manufacturer must register on the first taxable supply regardless of threshold to claim input-VAT credits on raw meat materials, processing utilities, packaging, fixed assets and export-related services. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Egyptian consumers are separately required to register once annual supplies to Egypt exceed EGP 500,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance is mandatory for all VAT-registered enterprises in Egypt. Every B2B invoice must be transmitted to the ETA e-invoicing platform (invoicing.eta.gov.eg) in XML format, digitally signed using an ETA-compliant electronic signature certificate, and cleared by the ETA before or at the time of issuance; the ETA returns a unique system-approved UUID and a machine-readable QR code for the final legal invoice. Integration is via REST API with OAuth2 authentication or SFTP bulk upload. B2C supplies are covered by the parallel e-receipt system. An invoice not cleared by the ETA is legally ineffective for input-VAT deduction, export zero-rating and customs audit evidence. Non-compliance penalties start at EGP 20,000 per un-cleared invoice, and can escalate to suspension of the taxpayer's e-invoicing account and denial of input-VAT recovery for the audit period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21(1) of the Egyptian VAT Law 67/2016, tangible goods physically exported from Egypt are zero-rated at 0% provided that: (a) the seller is a VAT-registered Egyptian taxpayer; (b) the export is made under an Egyptian Customs export declaration through an Egyptian exit port or airport; (c) the foreign-currency export proceeds are received in Egypt by the exporter's CBE-licensed bank within the mandatory 180-day repatriation period; (d) the ETA-cleared e-invoice reflects the 0% rate and the export transaction; and (e) the full customs, transport and banking documentation is retained for ETA audit. Freeze-dried pet raw meat and meal kibble falls within Chapter 2309/HS 2309.10 and qualifies for export zero-rating as a physical export of finished goods, provided the consignment clears Egyptian Customs (NAFIZA) and is loaded for carriage to a non-resident customer. Offshore services physically performed and consumed outside Egypt may also be zero-rated or treated as outside the VAT scope under Articles 20-22 of the VAT Law, but they are secondary to the zero-rated physical export of the manufactured pet-food goods in this dossier.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration processed through the NAFIZA single window, showing the exporter code, the HS 2309.10 commodity classification, net mass, value and the Egyptian exit port or airport, together with the customs release number
Bill of Lading (original clean-on-board set) or Air Waybill evidencing physical carriage of the freeze-dried pet-food consignment out of Egypt to the foreign buyer

Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the CBE-licensed bank documenting the foreign-currency export proceeds and the date of their credit to the exporter's Egyptian bank account within the 180-day window
Zero-rated VAT e-invoice (XML with ETA clearance code and QR) matching line-by-line the customs declaration, commercial invoice and export contract
Export sales contract or purchase order, final commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and the GOEIC/General Veterinary Organization export health certificate required for animal-origin pet food
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA audits export zero-rating claims by cross-matching NAFIZA customs export declarations, the CBE export-proceeds register, bank statements and the e-invoice archive. If the exporter fails to prove physical export, fails to evidence receipt of the foreign-currency proceeds in Egypt within 180 days (or any CBE-approved extension), or presents incomplete or false documentation, the ETA retroactively re-characterizes the supply at the standard 14% VAT and assesses the difference plus unified monthly simple delay interest at 1.5% (capped at 100% of the tax due) under Tax Procedures Law 206/2020, together with administrative fines which may reach EGP 100,000 per non-compliant invoice. Fraudulent zero-rating, including forged bills of lading, false customs declarations or manufactured inward remittance certificates, constitutes tax evasion under Articles 38-39 of VAT Law 67/2016 and carries criminal exposure of imprisonment and a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000 per violation, joint and several liability of the LLC's managers and UBOs, attachment of bank accounts, and cancellation of the exporter's e-invoicing and customs trader status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary, banking supervision, and foreign exchange authority under Law No. 88 of 2003, the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, and Law No. 38 of 1994 on Foreign Exchange; coordinated for investment registration and tax clearance with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: EGP is market-convertible on current-account items since the CBE's 6 March 2024 float and unified interbank rate: trade payments, service fees, royalties, and dividend remittances from audited distributable profits may be settled freely through authorized banks after documentary, customs, and tax-clearance verification. Capital-account convertibility is administrative: inbound FDI equity must be declared to the CBE under the balance-of-payments direct-investment code and funded via a local authorized bank; profit and capital exits require audited financial statements, ETA tax clearance, proof of the mandatory statutory reserve build-up under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (typically 5% of annual distributable profits), and a CBE foreign-currency transfer declaration. Practical hurdles are correspondent-bank de-risking and bank-level liquidity, not blanket exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE export-receipts framework (mid-2023 revision), proceeds from Egyptian manufactured exports must be credited to the exporter's account at an authorized bank within 270 days from the bill-of-lading/customs declaration date; capital goods receive an extended window. No mandatory conversion ratio is currently imposed - the LLC may retain 100% of proceeds in a foreign-currency account or voluntarily convert; however, every shipment must have a matching customs Form M/A-C entry and final invoice, and non-arrival of proceeds within 270 days triggers CBE credit sanctions, restriction of foreign-currency facilities, and auditor report qualification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow (Share Capital Deposit) Account / Operational EGP and USD Current Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational EGP and USD Current Account with Export Proceeds Sub-Account
Capital Escrow Account / Dual-Currency Operational and Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account with HSBC Global Correspondent Clearing
Capital Escrow Account / EGP and USD Operating Account with Dedicated Export Collections File

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary settlement rail; Medium as a supplementary rail for Platform_Pay and marketplace collections. Egypt's Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 requires all payment-service providers to be licensed by the CBE; non-resident digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) hold no Egyptian banking license, cannot open CBE-supervised accounts, and cannot participate in the CBE-operated EG-RTGS reconciliation and settlement system. They may only support offshore receipts that are subsequently repatriated by bank transfer, which will be flagged as third-party or aggregator flows. Recommended architecture: local licensed PSP (Fawry or Paymob) for domestic and platform pay-ins into the LLC's main operating account, and a Tier-1 bank for all FX settlement; any offshore wallet must be disclosed in the AML/KYC file to avoid downstream bank refusal.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is mandatory for primary corporate signatories. The CBE's KYC and Anti-Money Laundering instructions (Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended) require face-to-face identification for new corporate clients; Tier-1 banks deny fully remote opening. The managing director or an authorized in-country manager must interview at the branch in Egypt, present original passports and the original commercial registration, and sign all bank mandates in person. Non-resident co-signatories may act via apostilled or legalized and Arabic-translated notarized power of attorney, but at least one Egyptian resident signatory with physical presence is always required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO concentration (100% foreign or mixed foreign ownership) and cross-border ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI Commercial Register extract; notarized Articles of Association; full beneficial-ownership chain to individuals per CBE declaration templates; passports and proof-of-address of every UBO; foreign shareholder's board resolution; home-bank reference letter; Arabic-translated legalized corporate documents; commitment to notify on any UBO change within 30 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news, sanctions screening hits, or high-risk jurisdiction touchpoints in the raw-meat and FDI supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Systematic sanctions screening output for all shareholders, directors, suppliers, and buyers; declaration restricting financial intermediation to OECD/GCC banks; executed supply-chain contracts; country-of-origin certificates; veterinary and sanitary permits; auditable fund-flow map showing no cash or crypto leg; external counsel legal opinion on sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory industry licensing not yet reflected in the commercial register (pet-food manufacturing; NFSA and GOVS permits still pending)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NFSA registration receipt under Food Safety Law No. 1/2017; GAFI pre-license approval; General Organization for Veterinary Services (GOVS) importation permits for raw meat; ISO 22000/HACCP certification; environmental impact clearance; bank undertaking incorporating staged fund release against license issuance milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared seed capital, projected transaction velocity, and the entity's operating history (new LLC, low minimum capital)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 12-month business plan; cash-flow and turnover projections reconciled to the ISIC 1080 production capacity; 3-6 months of shareholder's bank statements proving source of funds; audited or reviewed financials of the parent; executed offtake, supplier, and logistics contracts; tax card and ETA registration linking the wider tax compliance file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI equity is wire-transferred via SWIFT MT103/TT exclusively to the LLC's dedicated capital escrow account at a Tier-1 authorized bank (NBE, Banque Misr, or CIB). The remitter's instruction and SWIFT cover must cite: beneficiary EG_LLC; bank account details; purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment - Equity Participation in Egyptian LLC' under the CBE balance-of-payments direct-investment classification; and reference to the GAFI license and Commercial Register number. The receiving bank performs the CBE inward-transfer declaration, verifies the share subscription and board resolutions, and credits the escrow only after issuance of the bank share-capital deposit certificate and the updated Commercial Registry extract. Released funds may be used for trade settlements only after customs ACI/CargoX import pre-registration, and all later profit distributions must be cross-referenced to this initial inflow in CBE remittance declarations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails for raw-meat and freeze-drying equipment imports: (1) SWIFT MT103 for confirmed advance or open-account payments to low-risk suppliers, supported by pro-forma invoice, import permit, and ACI number; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600; sight or up to 180-day usance) issued by the Egyptian bank for first-time or higher-risk counterparties, requiring full-set bills of lading, veterinary or phytosanitary certificates, and NFSA import permits (essential for raw meat); (3) Documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for repeat suppliers to preserve cash conversion cycles. All outbound settlements must be matched to customs Form M declarations and ACI electronic filings to avoid CBE penalties, and the LLC will maintain segregated USD and EGP pockets to minimize conversion leakage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (up to 12 months tenor) transacted through CBE-authorized dealing banks against documented import/export exposure; offshore NDFs are not licensable for onshore EG_LLC residents
USD/EGP FX swaps with authorized dealing banks for tenor-matched working-capital bridges, executed through the CBE interbank dealing system
Plain-vanilla currency options or synthetic collars on a bank treasury proprietary basis where the underlying trade forecast is firm and benchmarked to the unified interbank rate
Natural hedging via full statutory retention of export proceeds in foreign currency and matching USD, GBP, and EUR payable legs in the same currency corridors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the financial year-end; calendar-year companies must file by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to EGP 50,000 plus late-payment penalty of 2% per month on unpaid tax; prolonged non-filing may trigger enforced assessment and suspension of tax clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew blocks issuance of tax-clearance certificates, prevents execution of government contracts and import/export formalities, and may expose the entity to administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial-register renewal and declaration of current particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry / General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March; also within 30 days of any change in registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment of renewal fee results in an inactive commercial-register record; repeated non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All limited liability companies are required to appoint an independent auditor licensed in Egypt and to present audited annual financial statements to the partners’ assembly; there is no small-company exemption under the companies law. Foreign-investment LLCs must also file audited accounts with GAFI when requested.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are largely converged with IFRS; IFRS as issued by the IASB is acceptable for consolidated financial reporting of listed groups and financial institutions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a register of ultimate beneficial owners at its head office and update it within 30 days of any transfer of membership quotas or change in control. No standalone annual UBO return is required in Egypt for a private LLC, but the annual commercial-register renewal and corporate income tax return require the current ownership and beneficial-ownership information to be accurate and contemporaneous; non-update may attract AML/CFT penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Partners’ and Managers’ Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying manufacturing projects under Investment Law 72/2017 may deduct up to 50% of capital expenditure from taxable profits for a 7-year period; accelerated depreciation on freeze-drying and refrigeration equipment; export-related income benefits under Export Promotion Law 173/2022; small and medium enterprises under Law 152/2020 with annual turnover not exceeding EGP 20 million may elect a presumptive turnover-based tax of 0.5% for manufacturing activities. No blanket CIT holiday applies outside licensed free-zone or special economic zone status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 50, filed mandatorily through the Egyptian Tax Authority E-Services Portal (https://eta.gov.eg), together with the Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form and audited financial statements; large taxpayers use the dedicated Large Taxpayers Center channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly CIT advance payments and monthly withholding tax filings remitted through designated Egyptian banks)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a taxpayer with a 31 December year-end, the return is due by 30 April of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, Commercial Registry number, ETA tax card number, head-office address and activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Egyptian ETA tax card number of the EG_LLC; do not substitute the foreign parent's identification; state the ISIC 1080 manufacturing activity accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year period covered by the return, including any approved change in year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mirror the accounting period reflected in the statutory audit report signed by the Egyptian licensed auditor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and revenues: total Egyptian-source and export invoiced value of freeze-dried pet raw meat products, net of VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile export proceeds to Swift_TT and Platform_Pay settlement statements; flag any related-party purchases or sales for transfer-pricing reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: raw meat inputs, freeze-drying consumables, packaging, direct labour and production overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach customs release documents for imported frozen raw meat; inter-company purchases must be supported by an arm's-length study and, if applicable, the TP disclosure form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent, utilities, salaries, logistics, marketing, insurance and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All management fees and intra-group services charged by foreign affiliates must be documented with invoices, proof of actual services, and evidence of Egyptian withholding tax payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortization computed in accordance with Egyptian tax norms, including freeze-dryers, cold storage and industrial property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include tax non-deductible foreign head-office general overhead; allocate depreciation solely for assets physically located and used in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book profit or loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the net figure ties to the audited income statement; any foreign-currency revaluation gains on shareholder loans must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction declaration and transfer-pricing disclosure tick-box and annexure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the ETA transfer-pricing disclosure form if aggregate related-party transactions equal or exceed EGP 1 million; select the TP method applied and list all foreign counterparties and jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary tax adjustments: disallowed entertainment, donations, penalties, excess provisions, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back royalties and interest paid abroad if the 20% withholding was not effected; deduct wages but not employer payroll provisions unless actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after adjustments, prior to loss carryforward relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only confirmed loss carryforwards within the 5-year statutory limit; documentation of the prior-year loss assessment is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT liability at the statutory rate of 22.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that no free-zone or investment-incentive deduction is claimed without a prior written approval from the ETA and the General Authority for Investment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: quarterly CIT advance payments, foreign withholding tax credits, and final 10% dividend withholding credits where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach bank deposit receipts for quarterly advances and a schedule of 20% WHT recovered on inbound royalties/interest; foreign tax credits require a certified tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund carried to the ETA assessment file.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final payment must be settled through an Egyptian bank before any dividend repatriation; non-resident shareholders cannot receive distributions until this box is fully paid and cleared.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 50 triggers a fixed fine in the range of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000; late payment of the assessed tax triggers a monthly additional tax surcharge of 2% of the unpaid amount (capped at 30%), applied monthly rather than daily; wilful failure to file allows the ETA to make an ex-officio estimated assessment with a further discretionary penalty of up to the tax evaded, and criminal referral may result in imprisonment of responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding tax on gross distributions made by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholder (domestic intercompany participation exemptions may apply only where strict Egyptian corporate shareholding conditions are met).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Egyptian LLC an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty partner's competent tax authority, together with a valid beneficial ownership declaration, share register extract, and supporting ownership history; the Egyptian LLC must then file the application with the ETA before the dividend is distributed. Upon ETA approval the payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source; if the reduced rate is not approved in advance, the statutory 10% is withheld and the non-resident must claim a refund through the ETA within the 5-year time-bar, and the remitting bank requires an ETA tax clearance certificate before effecting any Swift_TT transfer out of Egypt.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic WHT rates for payments to non-residents not operating through a permanent establishment in Egypt: royalties 20% and interest 20% of the gross amount. Treaty-reduced rates under Egypt's double tax conventions generally range from 10% to 15% for both royalties and interest, subject to TRC submission, beneficial ownership analysis, and the Egyptian withholding agent's obligation to obtain ETA pre-approval for the preferential rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 1 million aggregate related-party transactions in a tax year triggers the mandatory transfer pricing disclosure form filed with Form No. 50; EGP 10 million aggregate related-party transactions triggers the preparation of a full Local File; membership in a multinational group with consolidated group turnover above EGP 200 million triggers a Master File, pursuant to ETA Decree No. 553 of 2018 and subsequent ETA TP guidelines; the ETA may also request contemporaneous documentation for smaller transactions under risk assessment.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations do not apply in Egypt; however, Egyptian tax law applies a substance-over-form doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements for treaty relief, and a general anti-avoidance rule under Article 30 of Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 96 of 2015. The EG_LLC must demonstrate substantive Egyptian operations and physical presence: board meetings, executive management, purchasing decisions, production, payroll, warehouse and banking transactions conducted in Egypt; inter-company service fees, royalties and interest are disallowed if no real activity, benefit or support to income generation is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording Platform_Pay or Swift_TT export receipts as personal remittances or shareholder loans instead of sales revenue; issuing fictitious supplier invoices for imported frozen raw meat; destroyed production and sales records understating freeze-dried product output.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex-officio assessment by ETA with full 22.5% CIT plus 2% monthly late-payment surcharge on the unpaid balance, a fine of double the evaded tax, a fixed fine of EGP 1,000 to EGP 10,000, publication of the taxpayer in the Egyptian Taxpayers Register, and criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers, directors and beneficial owners who directed or signed false returns may be personally assessed for the unpaid corporate tax, subjected to asset seizure and travel bans, and sentenced to imprisonment of up to 3 years; the corporate veil is pierced where fraudulent intent is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the EG_LLC as an invoice-passing shell with no Egyptian staff, no freeze-drying production line, no physical inventory, no utility consumption, and no local decision-making, while allocating the majority of profit to a foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA recharacterizes the transactions under the general anti-avoidance rule, disallows inter-company deductions, raises the assessed taxable income at 22.5% plus the 2% monthly surcharge, and may refer the case to the General Authority for Investment for deregistration and license revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders are jointly and severally liable for the reassessed tax and penalties; travel bans and closure of Egyptian bank accounts apply; directors may be barred from serving on any Egyptian board for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit Stripping through Excessive Interest and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing patent, trademark and know-how license fees of 30-40% of gross revenue to a tax-haven affiliate without any transfer pricing study, beneficial ownership file or ETA withholding approval, while simultaneously failing to withhold the statutory 20% on interest and royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the full deduction and recalculation of CIT at 22.5%; penalty on the Egyptian payer equal to the under-withheld WHT amount and an additional fine of up to 50% of the unreported remittance; monthly surcharges accrue until settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the distribution of dividends out of artificially reduced profits are personally liable for the shortfall in tax; remitting banks freeze further cross-border transfers; the responsible officers face criminal prosecution and imprisonment of up to 2 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Labeling Platform_Pay settlements as 'personal gifts' or 'family maintenance' to circumvent Egyptian bank Swift_TT controls, avoid ETA tax clearance certification, and conceal dividend or supplier payments to foreign persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended, financial penalties of EGP 100,000 to EGP 2,000,000, forfeiture of the transferred value, freezing of the entity's accounts, and referral by the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit to the public prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and directors who authorized or failed to disclose the wire structures face criminal imprisonment of 6 months to 7 years, confiscation of assets, placement on the Egyptian sanction list, and permanent restriction from holding banking mandates in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: CIT Non-Filing and Disappearance from Commercial Register
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form No. 50 for two consecutive fiscal years; abandoning the Egyptian commercial registration, failing to appoint an Egyptian tax representative, and omitting the requisite beneficial ownership disclosure with GAFI and the Commercial Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA issues a decreed estimated assessment on presumed profit, applies the 22.5% rate plus 2% monthly surcharge, levies fixed penalties up to EGP 40,000, suspends the Commercial Registry certificate, blocks import/export entitlements, and initiates compulsory liquidation proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid payroll taxes and WHT amounts not remitted; absence of the ETA tax clearance certificate imposes travel bans and prevents any sale or transfer of the company; managers may be personally sued for damages by creditors and investigated for criminal non-compliance.
